programmatic_narrative: Model cogito_32b_output was evaluated on 500 tasks. Mean coverage: 0.1036, median: 0.0. 498 tasks (99.6%) scored below the 1.0 threshold. Clean runs: 500, max tool calls errors: 0, max turns errors: 0, timeouts: 0. Failure categories: tool_call=239 (48.0%), cognitive=259 (52.0%). Top failure modes: no_tool_use (126), task_misunderstanding (119), early_termination (93).
llm_narrative: Across the 500 evaluation tasks, cogito_32b_output achieved a mean claim‑coverage of only 10.36 % (median 0 %) and passed just 2.2 % of cases at the ≥75 % coverage threshold, indicating that the model reliably completed virtually none of the multi‑step, tool‑driven queries. The dominant failure modes were cognitive: 126 instances (25.2 %) involved no tool use, 119 (23.8 %) stemmed from task misunderstanding, and 93 (18.6 %) ended in early termination; together these three categories account for roughly two‑thirds of all failures. Tool‑related breakdowns were less frequent but still significant—84 cases (16.8 %) used the wrong tool and 30 (6 %) produced malformed calls, contributing to a total of 239 tool‑call errors (48 % of all failures) versus 259 purely cognitive errors (52 %). The clearest actionable improvement is to enforce a “tool‑first” validation layer that checks whether at least one successful tool call has been made before the model proceeds to synthesis, and to add an automated retry/recovery loop for malformed or failed calls. What sets cogito_32b_output apart from other models in this benchmark is its relatively clean runtime environment (zero infra errors) combined with a systematic inability to translate retrieved data into final answers, as evidenced by the high proportion of cognitive mis‑steps and premature exits rather than execution failures.
